meta.use_note: Operational summary of climate-resilient agriculture measures for advisory generation. Validate and refine entries against the official compendium during technical review.

default: Coordinate field validation with MAO/AEWs before public release.
Prioritize advisories for vulnerable rainfed and smallholder production areas.
Document farm impacts for DA and PCIC support where losses are observed.

PAGASA_TCWS_ACTIVE: Secure harvested produce, seed stocks, fertilizer, machinery, and livestock shelters before strong winds arrive.
Conduct early harvest for mature rice, corn, and HVCC where safe.
Prepare drainage outlets and post-event damage assessment forms with MAO and MDRRMC.
POSTHARVEST_DRYING_RISK: Use mechanical dryers, covered drying floors, tarpaulins, and ventilated temporary storage.
Prioritize hauling of wet palay/corn to postharvest facilities to avoid quality losses.
Monitor grain moisture before storage and milling.
IRRIGATION_HIGH_DEMAND: Schedule supplemental irrigation for reproductive-stage rice/corn and high-value crops first.
Apply alternate wetting and drying in irrigated rice fields where appropriate.
Mobilize small farm reservoirs, pumps, and water-harvesting facilities for rainfed areas.
WET_SPELL_DISEASE_WATCH: Improve drainage and avoid prolonged waterlogging in low-lying fields.
Increase pest and disease scouting for fungal and bacterial disease triggers.
Use resistant varieties and integrated pest management; spray only during safe weather windows.
RAIN_EXTREME_24H: Clear canals, drainage lines, spillways, and field outlets before additional rainfall.
Move inputs and harvested crops to elevated, dry storage.
Monitor flood-prone barangays and prepare seed buffer support for replanting.
RAIN_HARVEST_RISK: Defer harvest and open-field drying until rainfall risk lowers, unless crop maturity requires emergency harvest.
Use covered transport and drying facilities for wet grain.
Coordinate shared dryers, tarpaulins, and storage space through MAO and farmer groups.
DROUGHT_CRITICAL: Prioritize water rationing, supplemental irrigation, and emergency pumps for reproductive-stage crops.
Shift vulnerable rainfed areas to short-duration or drought-tolerant varieties where replanting is needed.
Activate damage validation, PCIC coordination, seed buffer planning, and water-harvesting support.
DROUGHT_WARNING: Promote moisture conservation through mulching, shallow cultivation, and weed control.
Adjust planting windows and avoid new rainfed planting without reliable rainfall outlook.
Inspect communal irrigation, small water impounding, and pump availability.
DROUGHT_WATCH: Monitor soil moisture proxies and crop wilting signs in rainfed barangays.
Advise farmers to conserve water and prepare supplemental irrigation options.
Use climate-resilient varieties and staggered planting where feasible.
HEAT_DANGER: Shift farm labor to early morning or late afternoon and provide water/rest breaks.
Increase irrigation or moisture conservation for heat-sensitive crop stages.
Provide shade, ventilation, and water for livestock and poultry.
HEAT_HIGH: Avoid strenuous field operations during peak heat hours.
Monitor flowering/tasseling crops for heat stress and maintain soil moisture.
Use heat-tolerant varieties in future planting where locally suitable.
FERTILIZER_DEFER: Defer fertilizer application before heavy rain to prevent nutrient loss and runoff.
Apply split fertilizer doses when field conditions improve.
Keep fertilizer stocks dry and elevated.
SPRAYING_DEFER: Defer pesticide or foliar spraying during rain, strong wind, or very high humidity.
Resume only during calm, dry windows and follow label safety intervals.
Strengthen pest scouting and non-chemical IPM while spraying is delayed.
BELOW_NORMAL_RAINFALL: Review crop calendar and planting decisions against seasonal rainfall outlook.
Prioritize drought-tolerant seed, water harvesting, and supplemental irrigation investments.
Rank rainfed municipalities for seed buffer, crop insurance, and livelihood diversification support.
